definitions.gloss: frank advice; candid counsel; honest admonition
definitions.explanation: Honest, straightforward advice given out of genuine concern for someone, even if it is difficult to hear. Often implies the advice is unpleasant but well-intentioned.

examples.english: Frank advice is hard to hear.

examples.japanese: ⟦{友人|ゆうじん}→友人：03649_yuujin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{忠言|ちゅうげん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{素直|すなお}→素直：00391_sunao⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{受|う}け{入|い}れた→受け入れる：05755_ukeireru⟧。
examples.english: I honestly accepted my friend's candid advice.

examples.japanese: ⟦{部下|ぶか}→部下：06453_buka⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{忠言|ちゅうげん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{耳|みみ}を{傾|かたむ}ける→耳を傾ける：06903_mimiwokatamukeru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できる→できる：00557_dekiru⟧⟦リーダー→リーダー：24312_riidaa⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{信頼|しんらい}される→信頼する：22988_shinraisuru⟧。
examples.english: A leader who can listen to frank advice from subordinates earns trust.

notes:
Composed of {忠|ちゅう} ('loyalty, faithfulness') and {言|げん} ('words, speech'). The word carries the nuance that the advice comes from a place of loyalty and genuine concern, even though it may be unpleasant to receive.

The famous proverb {忠言|ちゅうげん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{耳|みみ}→耳：01513_mimi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{逆|さか}らう→逆らう：02106_sakarau⟧ (frank advice grates on the ear) captures the essence of this word — honest counsel is often unwelcome but valuable. This proverb originates from Chinese classics.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {忠言|ちゅうげん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{呈|てい}する→呈する：12003_teisuru⟧: to offer frank advice (formal)
- {忠言|ちゅうげん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{従|したが}う→従う：02059_shitagau⟧: to follow candid counsel
- {忠言|ちゅうげん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{無視|むし}する→無視する：17288_mushisuru⟧: to ignore frank advice
- {忠言|ちゅうげん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{耳|みみ}→耳：01513_mimi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{逆|さか}らう→逆らう：02106_sakarau⟧: frank advice grates on the ear (proverb)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{助言|じょげん}→助言：05461_jogen⟧: advice — neutral and general; does not carry the connotation of being unpleasant
- {諫言|かんげん}: remonstrance — more formal; specifically advising a superior against a wrong course of action
- ⟦{忠告|ちゅうこく}→忠告：05462_chuukoku⟧: warning, admonition — similar meaning but slightly less literary; more common in everyday use
